title: Chapter 43 — Hark!
paragraphs: "Hey! Did you hear that noise, Cabaco?"

It was the middle watch. A fair moonlit night. The seamen were standing in a line, passing buckets from one of the freshwater barrels amidships to the drinking cask near the stern. Standing mostly on the sacred ground of the quarterdeck, they were careful not to speak or scuffle their feet. From hand to hand the buckets went in the deepest silence, broken only by the occasional flap of a sail and the steady hum of the never-stopping engine room of the sea.
It was in the midst of this quiet that Archy, one of the line, whose post was near the after-hatches, whispered to his neighbor, a Chilean, the words above.
"Hey! Did you hear that noise, Cabaco?"
"Take the bucket, will you, Archy? What noise do you mean?"
"There it is again — under the hatches — don't you hear it — a cough — it sounded like a cough."
"Cough be damned! Pass along that return bucket."
"There again — there it is! — it sounds like two or three sleepers turning over!"
"Good lord! Knock it off, shipmate, will you? It's the three soaked biscuits you ate for supper turning over inside you — nothing else. Watch the bucket!"
"Say what you want, shipmate. I've got sharp ears."
"Right, you're the one, aren't you, who heard the hum of the old Quaker lady's knitting needles fifty miles at sea from Nantucket. You're the one."

"Grin away. We'll see what turns up. Listen, Cabaco — there is somebody down in the after-hold who has not yet been seen on deck. And I suspect our old captain knows something about it too. I heard Stubb tell Flask, one morning watch, that there was something of that sort going on."
